Paybacks Raises $10M Pre-Series A From Foresight Ventures
summary:
Paybacks today announced a $10 million Pre-Series A investment from Foresight Ventures and the official launch of paybacks.io, a platform that returns a portion of crypto futures trading fees to traders as cashback.
Foresight Ventures is the sole investor in the round, acquiring a 10% stake at a $100 million valuation. The funding announcement and platform launch come as Paybacks begins offering its cashback service through agreements with participating crypto exchanges.
Under a typical exchange referral arrangement, the exchange pays a commission based on trading fees generated by users who joined through a partner’s link. Paybacks uses the commissions it receives under its exchange agreements to provide cashback to the traders whose activity generated them. Depending on the applicable rate, eligible traders can receive up to 90% of their futures trading fees back.
Cashback is credited automatically in USDT to a trader’s exchange account the day after an eligible trade. For a trader who pays $1,000 in eligible fees, the maximum rate would mean $900 in cashback. The amount received depends on the rate applicable to that trader’s exchange account.
Paybacks is also launching with its Highest Cashback Guarantee. If a trader finds a higher cashback rate elsewhere, Paybacks says it will match that rate under the guarantee.
To use the platform, a trader signs up for a participating exchange through Paybacks and links their exchange UID. Once the account is linked, eligible trading activity generates cashback for payment the following day. Paybacks offers 24-hour live support, including assistance for traders seeking to move an existing exchange account, and plans to add more exchanges after launch.

title: OpenWay Joins Visa Digitalization Ready Program to Accelerate Digital Payment Adoption in Asia Pacific
summary:
OpenWay, a global provider of digital payment software and developer of the Way4 platform, has joined the Visa Digitalization Ready Program (VDRP) in Asia Pacific. The collaboration with Visa, a world leader in digital payments, supports financial institutions in implementing eligible Visa digital payment solutions, with an initial focus on Visa Flexible Credential and Click to Pay.
Through the program, OpenWay and Visa aim to accelerate client implementations, expand adoption of Visa payment capabilities and create additional business opportunities for their mutual clients across the region. Participation strengthens OpenWay’s ability to help banks, processors and fintechs bring new payment services to market on Way4, translating payment innovation into practical benefits for consumers and businesses.
Financial institutions face a dual challenge: responding to demand for more convenient digital payments while managing the cost and complexity of introducing new services. Customers increasingly expect greater control over how they pay and straightforward online checkout. Meeting these expectations requires coordination between payment networks, technology providers and the institutions delivering the customer experience.
VDRP supports the implementation of eligible Visa digital payment solutions in Asia Pacific. OpenWay’s participation brings this support together with Way4’s capabilities in card issuing, transaction processing and digital payments, helping clients move from product planning to implementation more efficiently.
“Visa is focused on making e-commerce seamless and secure for customers, merchants and financial institutions,” said Krishna Thiruvengadam, Head of Core Platform & Digital Solutions. “OpenWay’s participation in the Visa Digitalization Ready Program brings together Visa’s digital payment capabilities and Way4’s processing platform to help accelerate deployment of these digital innovations across Asia Pacific. Starting with Visa Flexible Credential and Click to Pay, we see a strong opportunity to help our mutual clients create differentiated payment experiences and unlock new opportunities for growth.”
“Financial institutions want to turn payment innovation into services that customers choose to use every day,” said Rudy Gunawan, Managing Director of OpenWay Asia. “Joining the Visa Digitalization Ready Program strengthens our collaboration with Visa in Asia Pacific and helps our clients bring these services to market more efficiently. Our initial focus brings together two clear customer benefits: greater flexibility in how people fund their purchases and less effort when they pay online.”
Greater payment choice through one credential
Visa Flexible Credential enables a single payment credential to provide access to multiple funding sources. Depending on the issuer’s offering, customers can use it to access options such as debit or credit, with choices managed through their financial institution.
For cardholders, this creates a more convenient way to use different payment options through a familiar credential. It gives issuers opportunities to design innovative propositions around customers’ financial needs, connect distinct existing products and offer additional services within their banking relationship.
Way4 supports the processing and configuration capabilities financial institutions need to develop these propositions. OpenWay’s participation in VDRP supports client implementation of Visa Flexible Credential, helping issuers translate payment flexibility into differentiated products for their markets.
Easier online payments with Click to Pay
Click to Pay simplifies online checkout by enabling consumers to pay with enrolled cards without having to repeatedly enter their card details at participating merchants. It addresses a familiar source of friction in digital commerce: the effort required to find a card and complete payment forms.
For issuers, Click to Pay can support customer engagement and card usage by making their cards easier to use online. For merchants, a simpler checkout experience can help reduce cart abandonment and make it easier for customers to complete their purchases. Consumers benefit from a more consistent way to pay across participating online stores, with security built into the payment experience.
Way4 already supports Visa Click to Pay. OpenWay’s participation in VDRP builds on this foundation to support client implementations and wider adoption across Asia Pacific, helping more financial institutions offer Click to Pay to their cardholders and incorporate it into their digital payment offerings.
Supporting continued innovation on Way4
Joining VDRP advances OpenWay’s strategy of helping clients develop and scale payment services on a flexible platform. Way4 combines card issuing, merchant acquiring, digital wallets and transaction switching on a single real-time platform, giving financial institutions a foundation for expanding their payment businesses.
For processors serving multiple financial institutions, the ability to introduce new capabilities through a common platform is particularly valuable. For banks and fintechs, it supports a continuing product roadmap as customer needs and market opportunities evolve.
The initial scope of OpenWay’s VDRP participation covers Visa Flexible Credential and Click to Pay, with the potential to include additional eligible Visa solutions over time. The collaboration is focused on Asia Pacific and supports a shared objective: making it easier for financial institutions to implement payment capabilities that deliver meaningful customer value.

Government Reappoints AI Champions to Drive the Next Phase of AI in Financial Services
summary:
Technology experts Harriet Rees and Dr. Rohit Dhawan have been reappointed as the government’s Financial Services AI Champions until 2027, helping support the UK remain a global leader in the safe and innovative use of AI in financial services.
The two Champions will coordinate delivery of industry recommendations in the Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, helping accelerate safe and responsible adoption of AI and unlocking greater productivity and competitiveness across the sector.
The Economic Secretary Lucy Rigby will announce the reappointments of Ms Rees and Dr. Dhawan, of Starling Bank and Lloyds Bank respectively, today (25 November 2026) during a keynote speech at the techUK summit on AI sovereignty in financial services. Her speech will emphasise the importance of safe adoption of AI at scale and at pace, encouraging firms to test, deploy and scale AI while ensuring accountability remains clear.
AI is already transforming financial services, delivering better outcomes for consumers and supporting growth across the UK economy. The financial sector has been one of the fastest adopters of AI, with 86% of UK financial firms now having deployed AI systems.
Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Lucy Rigby KC MP, said:
From driving productivity and growth to helping to deliver better services, the safe adoption of AI is key to the future of financial services.
Harriet and Rohit have already proven their dedication to ensuring the UK remains a world leader in AI adoption across financial services, and I’m delighted both have accepted extensions to their terms of appointment.
AI is helping firms tackle fraud and financial crime, strengthen risk management and improve services for consumers, while creating significant opportunities to grow enterprise productivity. As the technology develops, the government is focused on ensuring firms of all sizes have the confidence, clarity and support needed to adopt AI safely and at scale, while maintaining high levels of public trust.
Since their appointment in January, the two Champions have brought together industry, regulators and other stakeholders to identify opportunities to build on the responsible use of AI. Their Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, published in July, set out practical recommendations to overcome barriers to adoption and ensure the UK remains an attractive place to develop, deploy and scale AI-enabled financial services.
The Champions will continue to draw on their deep industry networks and extensive expertise in this field to support and coordinate delivery of the Plan’s recommendations. They will continue to engage with firms and regulators to ensure voices across the sector are reflected in the UK’s approach to AI in financial services.
Harriet Rees, Group Chief Information Officer – Starling Bank, said: 
Being reappointed as AI Champion for Financial Services comes at a pivotal moment as the sector moves from ambition to delivery. Alongside HM Treasury, the regulators, and wider industry, I am focused on driving practical progress - unlocking the potential of agentic AI and modernised advice, while managing concentration risk and clarifying the regulatory perimeter. Getting this right will ensure AI exceeds customers’ expectations, unlocks sustainable growth across the UK’s regions, and reinforces our status as the world’s most technologically advanced financial centre.
Dr Rohit Dhawan, Head of AI and Advanced Analytics – Lloyds Banking Group, said:
The UK financial services sector is leading the way in AI adoption, and we have a real opportunity to turn that early lead into lasting economic advantage. Accelerating responsible adoption can boost productivity and growth, deliver better outcomes for consumers and businesses, and reinforce the UK’s position as a world-leading financial centre.
I’m looking forward to continuing as AI Champion and turning our recommendations into action. That means ensuring regulation, including the regulatory perimeter, keeps pace with AI. Strengthening resilience, building the skills our industry needs and unlocking the next wave of innovation in agentic payments will also be critical. Collaboration between industry, regulators and government will be essential to removing barriers, building trust and maximising the economic opportunity AI presents for the UK.
At Budget 2026, Chancellor John Healey set out Britain’s distinctive approach to AI; managing risks responsibly, ambitious about the opportunity, and backed by the institutions, capabilities and infrastructure needed to manage the transition.
This was supported with a £700 million package of investment across security, resilience and public trust by unlocking the opportunities of AI, making a new deal for data centres set out in a Data Centre Covenant, and building British capability in AI hardware.

Most Europeans Take Payment Security on Faith
summary:
Almost three quarters of Europeans (74%) trust their bank to keep their payments secure, but just 22% feel they understand how those payments are protected, according to new research from Enfuce, Europe's card issuing and processing powerhouse. The findings come from a survey of 4,000 adults in France, Germany, Italy and the Netherlands. That sense of safety offers little protection when a scam arrives.
Key findings
13% of consumers who feel they understand payment security well said they shared personal or payment details after a phishing email without losing money in the past two years, compared with 4% of those who feel they do not understand it well.
74% trust banks to keep their payments secure, but just 22% feel they understand well how that protection works.
41% would feel uncomfortable if AI handled fraud detection on their payments instead of a human team. Only 20% would feel comfortable.
Just 19% would trust AI to make or manage payments, the lowest level of trust among the ten everyday tasks surveyed.
Consumers trust banks but are less sure how their payments are protected
Almost three quarters of consumers (74%) trust banks to keep their payments secure, yet just 22% feel they understand well how those payments are protected. The findings suggest that people put their faith in the bank, even when they are less sure how it protects them. Fintech and payment apps do not inspire the same confidence: just 27% trust them to keep their payments secure.
Dutch consumers are the most trusting of banks, while Italians are least likely to feel they understand payment security well. Banks are trusted by 83% of consumers in the Netherlands, 71% in Germany and France, and 70% in Italy. Far fewer feel they understand payment security well: 27% in the Netherlands, 26% in Germany, 18% in France and 17% in Italy.
Consumers disagree on who should pay after a scam
More than half (53%) would contact their bank first after suspected payment fraud. But asking for help does not mean holding the bank responsible: only 13% think it should be mainly responsible for the loss when someone is tricked into paying a fraudster.
French consumers are more than twice as likely as German consumers to contact their bank first after suspected fraud (77% versus 38%), even though trust in banks is 71% in both countries.
The Dutch are the most likely to say the person who was tricked should be mainly responsible for the loss: 42% take that view, compared with 10% in Germany and 16% in France and Italy. Those who feel they understand payment security well are also more likely to hold this view (26%, compared with 18% among the less confident).
Few people would trust AI with their payments
Almost everyone (94%) would accept at least one extra safeguard for more secure payments, but only 13% would accept AI being used to detect fraud. Of the ten tasks tested, making or managing payments is where people trust AI least (19%).
Of the ten everyday tasks surveyed, making or managing payments is where consumers trust AI least. Just 19% would trust AI to help with payments, compared with 56% who would trust it as a search engine and 22% who would trust it for mental health or emotional support.
The main worry is that AI could make mistakes (46%). Asked what would most increase their trust in any payment method, consumers most often chose knowing they would get their money back if something went wrong (25%). The research suggests payment providers need to be clearer about what help people can expect if protection fails, and that protection.
“People should not need to be payment security experts to keep their money safe. Our research shows why protection cannot depend on how confident someone feels. It has to be built into the systems they use. AI can help strengthen that protection, but the industry has to earn people’s trust in it. Consumers need to know how their money is protected and who will put things right if something goes wrong. That responsibility stays with us as the technology changes.” Denise Johansson, CEO and Co-founder of Enfuce said.

The research, covering consumers in France, Germany, Italy, and the Netherlands, also highlights widespread distrust in artificial intelligence for fraud detection and payment management. Most consumers believe the individual tricked in a scam should share responsibility for losses.

title: Stablecoin Fees Could Add 10% to a $20 Purchase, Research Finds Ahead of Black Friday
summary:
Customers paying merchants directly from cryptocurrency exchanges could face significant additional costs when using stablecoins, according to new research from Orbital, ahead of Black Friday.
Around 70% of stablecoin checkout payments to Orbital’s merchants came directly from cryptocurrency exchanges rather than personal wallets, according to Orbital’s payment processing data for August to October 2026. Customers paying this way may face an exchange withdrawal fee when sending their payment, adding to the purchase price even though the charge sits outside the merchant’s checkout.
Orbital analysed 24.8 million withdrawals of USDT and USDC, the two most popular stablecoins, worth $184.7 billion from 11 major exchanges in October 2026 for its report, The Real Cost of Stablecoin Checkout, estimating total withdrawal fees of $17.3 million.
It found that high withdrawal fees could add a staggering 10% to a $20 purchase.
Key findings include:
Small checkout payments can carry disproportionately high fees
More than half (51%) of the exchange withdrawals analysed were worth less than $100, while over a third were below $50. 
Because exchanges often charge flat withdrawal fees, smaller transactions can be disproportionately expensive. At 3 November fees, the median Tron withdrawal fee of $1.50 adds 7.5% to a hypothetical $20 payment. At Binance’s $2 Tron withdrawal fee, recorded on 16 November, this rises to 10%. 
On the other hand, the median USDT withdrawal fee on BNB Chain was just one cent, based on exchange fees recorded on 3 November – equivalent to 0.05% of a $20 payment. For merchants accepting smaller purchases, offering lower-cost compatible networks could make stablecoin checkout payments more affordable.
The networks merchants accept can significantly affect payment costs
Tron handled 39% of the withdrawals analysed but generated 83% of estimated fees, worth approximately $14.4 million. BNB Chain processed a similar share of withdrawals, at 37%, but accounted for just 2.6% of fees. 
Withdrawal fees can change overnight 
On 1 November, Binance raised its Tron withdrawal fee from $1.50 to $4, before reducing it again to $2 by 16 November. 
Across 201 withdrawal routes compared between January and 3 November, 53 became more expensive and 59 became cheaper. On 3 November, 17% of listed withdrawal routes were paused, making them unavailable for transfers at that time. 
Costs also vary sharply between exchanges. In October, Crypto.com’s average withdrawal fee was $4.62 – more than eight times higher than Binance’s.
Choosing cheaper networks could cut withdrawal fees by 98%
Orbital estimates that total fees across the withdrawals analysed could have fallen from $17.3 million to approximately $340,000 if every withdrawal had used the cheapest available network for the same stablecoin on its exchange.
That represents a theoretical reduction of 98%, illustrating how much network choice can affect costs. 
Why this matters for merchants
As stablecoins become a more practical way to pay, businesses need to think about the costs customers face when using them. Orbital’s payment data shows that direct exchange-to-merchant transfers are already a meaningful use case, making withdrawal fees relevant to the overall cost of paying with stablecoins. 
The wider research covers exchange withdrawals generally, rather than merchant purchases alone. However, it highlights potential challenges as businesses explore stablecoins for consumer transactions. 
“While it’s too early to say how quickly direct exchange-to-merchant payments will grow, merchants need to be prepared as stablecoin payments become more popular,” said Luke Wingfield Digby, co-founder and Head of Corporate Development of Orbital. 
“Merchants can’t control exchange withdrawal fees, but they can offer customers a choice of compatible and lower-cost networks. Getting that right now could help make stablecoin checkout payments more affordable and easier to use as adoption grows, while reducing friction and potentially improving conversion.”
* The analysis covers exchange withdrawals generally, rather than merchant purchases alone.

content: New research from Orbital ahead of Black Friday reveals that stablecoin checkout payments made directly from cryptocurrency exchanges can incur high withdrawal fees. Because many customers pay via exchanges rather than personal wallets, flat withdrawal fees can add up to 10% to small purchases like a $20 transaction. Experts suggest merchants can reduce these costs by accepting lower-cost compatible blockchain networks.

Unzer Expands Ecosystem With Tap to Pay: Smartphones Become Payment Terminals and Cash Registers
summary:
Unzer, one of Europe’s leading payment and software solution providers, has launched Tap to Pay, a new solution aimed at small and medium-sized businesses. With Tap to Pay, any NFC-enabled Android smartphone can be turned into a fully functional payment terminal without the need for any additional hardware. Merchants simply need the Unzer app to accept contactless card payments or payments made by smartphone or smartwatch directly. The underlying technology is known as SoftPOS (Software Point of Sale).
 
With Tap to Pay, Unzer is responding to the growing demand for flexible and mobile payment solutions. The offering is particularly well-suited to hospitality businesses, food trucks, market stalls, service providers and small retailers who want to accept payments wherever their customers are.
 
What makes Unzer's solution unique is that Tap to Pay is available not only as a standalone payment solution, but also in combination with Unzer's POS software. This turns an Android smartphone into both a payment terminal and a mobile cash register. Merchants can record sales and accept payments on the same device, without the need for additional POS hardware or payment terminals. In restaurants, staff can also use a single smartphone to take orders directly at the table and then accept payments.
 

“Today, commerce happens everywhere: in-store, online and on the go. With Tap to Pay, we make the entry into digital payments easier than ever before: in just a few minutes, an Android smartphone can become not only a secure payment terminal but also a fully functional mobile POS system,” says Isabelle Bénard, Chief Product and AI Officer at Unzer.
 
The launch of Tap to Pay is another step in expanding Unzer’s ecosystem, which brings together payments, software, and financial services on a single platform. Recently, Unzer extended its offering to include Unzer Financial Services. The solution features a business account and a corporate credit card with no monthly account fees. Incoming payments are instantly available in the merchant’s business account, while all financial and payment data is consolidated within the UnzerOne dashboard.
 

“Every merchant should have access to the same digital tools to manage their business easily - regardless of their size. With Tap to Pay, we are adding a particularly simple and flexible way to accept payments anywhere,” says Bénard.
 
The new solution is available to merchants in Germany with immediate effect.
